name: Hughes
product_focus: HughesON managed SD-WAN for distributed enterprise
evidence_summary: Hughes sources evidence managed SD-WAN for distributed organisations and end-to-end turnkey network delivery.
cost_model: Quote-based managed service; site count, access mix, security, satellite/broadband/cellular and support model drive pricing.
key_differentiators: Strong specialism in distributed organisations with site count in the hundreds or thousands.
Multi-access mix including satellite, broadband and cellular suits remote or rural site profiles.
End-to-end turnkey delivery from design through field operations to ongoing support.
best_fit_for: Highly distributed enterprises (retail, restaurants, hospitality, fuel retail) with hundreds of sites.
Organisations with remote or rural sites where satellite access is required alongside terrestrial broadband.
Buyers wanting one provider for design, access, install and ongoing managed service.
watch_outs: SASE and SSE capabilities are largely partner-integrated; security depth should be confirmed.
Less suited to enterprise headquarters or data centre SD-WAN at large bandwidth scale.
Underlying SD-WAN platform should be confirmed; managed service wraps various vendor platforms.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason stated. Sources found and rejected are listed in the evidence register at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: AI-assisted network monitoring within the managed NOC.

resilience.note: Satellite plus terrestrial blended transport keeps remote sites online.

profile.platform_architecture: Hughes Network Systems, an EchoStar company, built its managed SD-WAN practice serving exactly the estates others find hard: thousands of distributed sites with mixed-quality access, blending broadband, cellular and its own satellite capacity (including JUPITER fleet assets) into managed connectivity. Platform delivery uses leading SD-WAN stacks (notably Fortinet) wrapped in Hughes managed operations.
profile.security_sase: Managed security wraps the platform stack (Fortinet-led) with Hughes SOC operations tuned for distributed retail-style estates: PCI-conscious segmentation, store-format repeatability and centralised policy. Depth follows the platform; the value is operating security uniformly across thousands of small sites.
profile.service_support_channel: Fully managed is the model: 24x7 NOC operations, field services at national scale in North America, and processes built for franchise and multi-banner estates. US-centred with international delivery via partners; UK presence is limited, so confirm in-region arrangements.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-site managed pricing tuned to high-volume small sites, quote based. The Netify verdict: shortlist Hughes for North American retail, restaurant, fuel and franchise estates measured in hundreds or thousands of sites, especially where satellite or cellular fills coverage gaps. It is a specialist: outside distributed-site use cases, generalist carriers fit better.

vendor_faqs.q: Why is Hughes strong in retail and franchise networks?
vendor_faqs.a: Decades of operating tens of thousands of small sites: cookie-cutter store designs, PCI-aware segmentation, national field services and a NOC built for volume. Few providers run distributed estates at that scale as the core business.

vendor_faqs.q: Does satellite still matter in SD-WAN?
vendor_faqs.a: For coverage gaps, yes: Hughes blends satellite with broadband and cellular so remote or rural sites join the same managed WAN with appropriate traffic steering, useful for fuel, agriculture and remote retail.

vendor_faqs.q: Can Hughes serve UK or European estates?
vendor_faqs.a: Primarily via partners; the operational depth is North American. UK-led estates with US store networks sometimes use Hughes for the US leg alongside a European provider.

shortlist_summary: Hughes have a background in satellite and large-scale retail deployment that means the operational model is genuinely built for distributed organisations with site counts in the hundreds or thousands. Typically shortlisted by businesses running a large estate of smaller sites, rather than a smaller number of complex locations, where that specific operational specialism matters more than the likes of SASE security depth.
cost_note: Per-site managed tuned to high-volume small sites; value for distributed retail estates.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK delivery via partners; specialism is distributed retail estates.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Fully Managed Solution: Ideal for businesses that are seeking expert support from a managed service provider with design, strategy, installation, configuration, monitoring, and ongoing management.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Corroborated on the Managed SD-WAN page ("Fully managed service delivery") and the Managed Router page ("Hughes monitors, manages, and maintains your network for you, bringing decades of expertise and industry-leading customer service to provide 24x7x365 support to your business."). Hughes operates the service end to end across design, install, monitoring and ongoing management.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: Our SOC works seamlessly with your existing security staff, augmenting their current capabilities and drastically increasing a team of any size's productivity.
f03_co_managed_service.note: No named co-managed tier with defined customer change rights was found. The Managed SASE solutions sheet lists three deployment options ("Fully Managed Solution", "SSE Investments in Place", "Standalone Offering"), of which "SSE Investments in Place: For businesses that need help in fully leveraging and optimizing their existing SSE investments." is the closest to shared responsibility. The MDR page describes the Hughes SOC augmenting in-house staff. Graded partial because shared policy and change rights are not documented.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Read the Hughes VAR / resellers page, which offers "The Hughes Value Added Resellers (VAR) program allows service operators, system integrators" and "Automated ordering portals for hardware and service", plus the What We Offer index. No language on tenant isolation, delegated administration, branded or white-label portals, or MSP templates was found on any Hughes page read.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Hughes has decades of experience as a managed services provider with exceptional engineering expertise and qualified staff to deploy, migrate, and manage the solution.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: The FortiSASE solutions sheet also states "Global Secure Connectivity: Extend corporate security policies to users anywhere in the world while Hughes handles onboarding, policy tuning, and user provisioning at scale." and the Netskope sheet covers design, strategy, installation and configuration. Discovery, pilots, runbooks, rollback plans and training are not itemised, but structured design and migration services are clearly offered.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: The Managed Routing offering includes router installation, configuration, maintenance, monitoring, help desk, billing, and management, plus end-to-end secure VPN tunneling from all sites.
f07_lifecycle_management.note: The Managed Router page also states "Responsive on-site field maintenance" and "Full range of services, from design to on-site support", and the May 2026 recognition article refers to Hughes strength spanning managed network services, security, monitoring, and lifecycle support. Graded partial because hardware replacement or RMA terms, firmware upgrade and patching cycles, renewals and end-of-life planning are not individually documented on the pages read.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: The Managed Wireless page also carries "Multi-carrier support", "Single & dual wireless transport options", "Secure your business wireless plans with backup and failover protection." and "Cellular connectivity provides higher availability options compared to wired broadband." The Managed Network Services page lists 4G LTE and 5G among all wireline transports, point-to-point microwave and satellite. SIM management and signal monitoring as discrete features were not documented, but primary and failover cellular transport is clearly supported.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Scalable Cloud Points of Presence: Low latency and high availability with Fortinet's distributed cloud infrastructure
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: The gateway and PoP estate is explicitly a third party's. The FortiSASE sheet attributes the cloud PoPs to Fortinet's distributed cloud infrastructure, and the Netskope sheet and Managed SSE page attribute the PoP network to Netskope. No evidence of Hughes operating its own terrestrial SASE gateway or PoP infrastructure was found, so this is partner_integrated rather than yes.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Read both Managed SASE solutions sheets (Netskope and FortiSASE), the Managed SASE page and the Managed SSE page. All PoP references describe shared global multi-tenant PoP networks belonging to Netskope or Fortinet. No customer-hosted, dedicated or sovereign PoP option was described anywhere.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Global Infrastructure: A vast network of global Points of Presence (PoPs) supports organizations with a reliable and scalable backbone for their security needs.
f21_private_global_backbone.note: The backbone described in this quote belongs to Netskope, since the document is the Managed SASE by Hughes, Powered with Netskope solutions sheet; the FortiSASE variant attributes equivalent infrastructure to Fortinet. Hughes does own and operate a GEO satellite fleet (JUPITER page: "Our fleet of satellites"), which is genuine owned transport, but no page read described a Hughes-owned or Hughes-controlled inter-region terrestrial backbone carrying traffic between PoPs. Graded partner_integrated on that basis.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: Industry-Leading SLAs: Boasting an impressive 10/50ms latency and 99.999% uptime, Hughes Managed SASE ensures consistent, high-performance connectivity.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Corroborated on the Managed Broadband page: "Service Level Agreements (SLAs), guaranteed Quality of Service (QOS), and Committed Information Rates (CIR)." Latency and uptime commitments are published. Response times and change-handling commitments were not found as published figures on the pages read.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Advanced Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Powered by artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), it monitors and protects sensitive data across websites, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) applications, emails, and platforms that use generative AI.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: DLP is fully described with classification, blocking and real-time enforcement (Managed SASE page: "DLP detects and blocks unauthorized sharing of sensitive information in real time, ensuring compliance and preventing data from leaving your network without explicit approval."), but the capability is Netskope technology delivered under the Hughes managed wrapper, so partner_integrated rather than yes. Exception workflows were not documented.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: With 24/7/365 SOC monitoring, comprehensive cybersecurity expertise, and resilient prevention, let Hughes mitigate advanced threats on your endpoints and servers that bypass prevention so you can focus on running your business.
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: 24/7 SOC and 24x7x365 network management are both evidenced (Managed Router: "24x7x365 management and support"), as is structured periodic reporting (MDR: "Receive monthly Executive Summary Reports detailing trends, updates, improvements and daily and weekly critical observations (depending upon service level)."). Graded partial because no page read documents formal root cause analysis ownership or change governance as contracted elements of the service.

delivery_model.quote: the largest non-carrier managed network services provider in North America
delivery_model.note: Confirmed verbatim on the page 29 Jul 2026. Hughes states it is explicitly non-carrier, which is why underlay ownership is graded separately below.

underlay_ownership.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The managed SD-WAN page states Hughes is non-carrier but does not say whether circuits are resold or customer-supplied.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Hughes has partnered with Fortinet to address these realities with a comprehensive Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) solution that brings together the advanced security capabilities of FortiSASE, with Hughes proven expertise in Managed Network Services.
sse_layer_ownership.note: Fortinet and Netskope. Hughes publishes two parallel Managed SASE solutions sheets, one Powered with FortiSASE and one Powered with Netskope ("Hughes has partnered with Netskope to address these challenges with a comprehensive Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) solution"). The Managed UTM and firewall layer additionally uses Cisco Meraki. Hughes contributes the managed operations wrapper, not the SSE stack itself.

regulatory_documentation.quote: Delivers peace of mind from knowing our next-generation SOC is ISO-certified
regulatory_documentation.note: ISO is claimed but the standard is not numbered, so this is an assurance statement rather than a named attestation. The same page names customer-facing compliance regimes it helps support, including Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance, HIPAA for patient information security and SOX for financial practices and corporate governance. Not found on any page read: ISO 27001 by number, SOC 2, NIS2, DORA or NHS DSPT. The Hughes UK solutions page was checked specifically and returned none of these. No trust centre or certification register entry was located.

pop_count.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Hughes describes "A vast network of global Points of Presence (PoPs)" in the Netskope solutions sheet and "Scalable Cloud Points of Presence" in the FortiSASE sheet, but publishes no numeric PoP count on any page or PDF read. The PoP estate in question belongs to Netskope or Fortinet in any case, not to Hughes.

sla_availability_pct.quote: Industry-Leading SLAs: Boasting an impressive 10/50ms latency and 99.999% uptime, Hughes Managed SASE ensures consistent, high-performance connectivity.
sla_availability_pct.note: Published by Hughes in the Managed SASE Powered with Netskope solutions sheet, alongside a 10/50ms latency commitment. The underlying platform SLA is Netskope's, surfaced through the Hughes managed wrapper. No equivalent percentage was published for Hughes Managed SD-WAN or Managed Broadband, where the Broadband page mentions SLAs, guaranteed QoS and CIR without any figure.

conflicts.claim_a: Hughes Managed SASE is powered with Netskope, whose SSE, DLP and global PoP network underpin the service
conflicts.claim_b: Hughes Managed SASE is powered with FortiSASE, with Fortinet supplying the security stack and distributed cloud Points of Presence

conflicts.claim_a: The Managed Cybersecurity page under Managed Network Services states the Hughes SOC is ISO-certified and discusses PCI, HIPAA and SOX
conflicts.claim_b: The current Managed Cybersecurity hub page contains no ISO, SOC 2, PCI or certification references at all
